recent_control_phase.source_note: The implementation owner changed an unrelated model category length bound after these tests completed. No implementation hash was captured at this phase start; historical implementation hashes are not inferred from the newer file.
coverage: A first-batch invalid closed tool argument produces one protocol_diagnostic_pause with persisted response/argument hashes; one already saved candidate survives and no retry, next batch or summary starts.
Two real Pi jobs in one process share one budget/store and identical source IR. Their HTTP streams overlap before stopping one job.
Both external cancellation and a short document deadline close only the stopped job stream; the healthy stream stays open until released and its job then completes.
Both jobs retain one candidate. The stopped job has one completed and one missing block; the healthy job has two completed blocks and a completed summary.

Events, run/task bindings and reopened records remain isolated. Each scenario shares exactly five requests (2+3), 33168 input tokens, 8272 output tokens and one conservative unknown-usage reservation.

limitations: Only the one actual category case and TypeScript checks were run after the latest field-bound change; all 43 runtime cases and unrelated suites were not repeated.
The earlier two control tests are separately preserved. Their starting implementation hash was not captured before a later edit, so historical implementation hashes are explicitly unavailable.
The actual real-paper failure and public safe arguments were produced by the implementation agent. This agent performed only local replay after the fix.
Concurrency validation covers two jobs in one process sharing one budget/store instance; it does not establish cross-process ledger coordination.
These engineering results do not establish clinical accuracy, medical recall, gold-annotation quality, real-provider latency or gateway billing correctness.
